items.headline: Ten ADU permits issued across San José in one week
items.summary: The city cleared ten accessory dwelling unit permits between Sept. 21 and 24, ranging from new detached units to garage conversions, with costs from about $77,000 to $186,000. The volume shows that ADUs remain a steady path for adding housing on existing lots, with a nearly even mix of new builds and garage conversions.

items.headline: City weighs legal action against major fire truck makers
items.summary: The City Council met in closed session to discuss a potential legal case against Golden State Fire Apparatus, Pierce Manufacturing, Oshkosh Corporation, REV Group, Rosenbauer America, and the Fire Apparatus Manufacturers' Association.

items.headline: Council discussed appointment of new City Attorney
items.summary: The council held a closed session item on a public employee appointment for the position of City Attorney.

items.headline: TIAA approved for three illuminated wall signs
items.summary: Architectural review cleared three illuminated wall signs for TIAA at 2875 El Camino Real, signaling the financial firm's branding for that location.

items.headline: Massage Envy gets new LED channel letter signs
items.summary: Two new LED channel letter wall signs were approved for Massage Envy at 2515 El Camino Real.

items.headline: Council held study session on Highway 17 congestion relief
items.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council held a study session on the State Route 17 Corridor Congestion Relief Project, a corridor well known to South Bay commuters for heavy traffic backups.
